name: Tashkent
blurb: The whole city, streamed in 1 km tiles as you go: 313,000 buildings, from the TV Tower to the old town.

name: Kokand
blurb: The old khanate capital of the Fergana Valley, whole: the khan's palace and the bazaar in the middle, and mile after mile of courtyard houses along the lanes.

name: Buvayda
blurb: A town north-east of Kokand: one main road, courtyard houses and orchards between the canals, and open country all round.

name: Yangiqo'rg'on
blurb: The seat of Buvayda district, between Kokand and Fergana (Ibrat on newer maps): a market town of low houses on a grid of lanes.

name: Uchko'prik
blurb: Three Bridges, a district town just east of Kokand: a dense core along the main road, fields and canals beyond.

name: Paris
blurb: Around the Eiffel Tower and the Seine: tight streets between tall stone blocks.

name: Tokyo
blurb: Tokyo Tower and Shiba: a dense mesh of small streets, houses and offices.

name: New York
blurb: Midtown Manhattan: a rigid street grid under skyscrapers.

name: Cairo
blurb: Downtown, near Tahrir Square and the Nile: crowded and thinly mapped.

name: London
blurb: Tower Bridge and the Thames: old lanes, new glass, and a river that splits the map.

name: Sydney
blurb: Circular Quay and the Opera House: a harbour edge, with the city piled up behind it.

name: Oia
blurb: A cliff-top village on Santorini: white houses, one long path, nowhere to run.
